definition: ETL vs ELT is a core concept in Data Analytics. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What ETL vs ELT is
theory.body: ETL vs ELT describes the methods and patterns used within Data Analytics to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: ETL vs ELT is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why ETL vs ELT matters
theory.body: Without ETL vs ELT, systems built with Data Analytics are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How ETL vs ELT works
theory.body: The mechanism behind ETL vs ELT follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of ETL vs ELT.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of ETL vs ELT
theory.body: ETL vs ELT offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
